data.title: Load Testing
data.tagline: Load testing measures latency, throughput, and errors while a system handles a realistic level of load.
data.learningOutcome: You can state a load scenario, signals, thresholds, and the evidence needed to verify an improvement.
data.description: Before an event, an isolated production-like environment can simulate browsing and checkout with synthetic or sanitized data. The team records response time, throughput, and failures, then compares them with predefined thresholds to decide what to improve. Load testing is not the same as pushing a system to its breaking point with stress testing, and it cannot promise zero production failures.

learning.assumes: You know that slow pages, failed requests, and a system's processing capacity are related.
learning.outcome: You can state a load scenario, signals, thresholds, and the evidence needed to verify an improvement.

explanation.title: Make the test scenario repeatable
explanation.text: “Simulate many people” is not enough. State the user actions, load volume or request rate, duration, environment, and data type. A production-like environment with synthetic or sanitized data supports a realistic judgment without touching real customer data.

explanation.title: Let signals choose the next iteration
explanation.text: Record latency, throughput, and error rate and compare them with predefined thresholds. If checkout slows or fails as load rises, locate and improve the bottleneck, then rerun the same scenario. Better results show that this change helped, but only for the tested conditions.

explanation.title: A second scenario: an online class
explanation.text: Before class starts, simulate students joining the live room and submitting answers at the same time. At the target attendance, record join latency, submission throughput, and errors, then rerun under the same conditions after improvements.

data.boundary: Load testing asks how a system behaves at a target or expected load. Stress testing generally pushes beyond that load to observe limits or failure modes. A passing load test covers only its environment, data, scenario, and time window; it cannot prove every production traffic pattern, dependency, or failure combination is safe.

lessonPractice.title: Before an event, checkout load testing shows 95th-percentile (p95) latency above threshold and rising errors. Which response is most useful?

options.label: Keep the scenario and metrics, locate the bottleneck, improve it, rerun, and compare the results
options.feedback: Correct. Load testing is useful when repeatable load and thresholds expose a bottleneck and the next run verifies the improvement.

options.label: Test one request once; if it succeeds, full-event checkout will not time out
options.feedback: One request applies no target load and cannot show latency, throughput, or errors under concurrency.

options.label: Exclude failed requests and report only the average response time of successful requests
options.feedback: Excluding failures hides the real impact under load; errors and latency must be analyzed for the same complete scenario.

data.agentPrompt: Design a load test for the event checkout flow. Use an isolated production-like environment with synthetic or sanitized data, simulate browsing, cart, and checkout, and define thresholds before recording latency, throughput, and error rate. After the test, report bottlenecks, original results, and repeated results after improvement; do not send test traffic to production.
